source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
Several scale insects (ថៃក្រមូន) attack citrus bark, leaves, and fruit, feeding by sucking sap and, in heavy infestations, weakening branches and blemishing fruit. The source describes green scale (ថៃក្រមូនពណ៌បៃតង, Coccus viridis, family Coccidae), a soft scale that clusters on stems and leaves; red scale (ថៃក្រមូនក្រហម, Aonidiella aurantii, family Diaspididae), which forms hard reddish-brown shell-like covers on bark, leaves and fruit; and purple scale (ថៃក្រមូនពណ៌ស្វាយ, Lepidosaphes beckii, family Diaspididae), a mussel-shaped scale that also infests bark and fruit, and is noted as sometimes moving over from nearby avocado (ប៉ែ, Avocado) trees.

Scale insects excrete sticky honeydew that ants feed on, and ants in turn protect scale colonies from natural predators in exchange for this food source - so controlling ant populations around infested trees is part of an effective management approach, alongside encouraging natural predators, pruning out heavily infested twigs, and applying appropriate insecticide or horticultural oil sprays when infestations are heavy.
